name: Sterling-Nakamura Autonomous Hunter-Killer Drone AHK-7 'Wolfhound'
description: A medium-sized autonomous combat drone the size of a large dog, equipped with a 5.56mm automatic weapon, thermal/optical sensor suite, and an AI capable of independent target acquisition and engagement. The Wolfhound can operate for 8 hours on a single charge, patrol a designated area autonomously, and engage targets matching its programmed threat profile without human authorization. It moves on four articulated legs that allow it to navigate rubble, stairs, and rough terrain that would defeat wheeled or tracked platforms. Sterling-Nakamura markets it as a 'persistent security presence' for high-value installations.
specifications:
armament: 5.56mm automatic, 300-round internal magazine
sensor suite: Thermal + optical + acoustic + motion
autonomous operation: 8 hours patrol, 2 hours active engagement
locomotion: Four articulated legs, 25 km/h maximum
weight: 35 kg
AI capability: Independent target acquisition and engagement
threat profiling: Programmable ROE with biometric whitelist
armor: Resistant to handgun calibers
communications: Encrypted mesh network with other AHK units
story_hooks: A pack of Wolfhound drones has gone rogue after their command facility was destroyed — they are still following their last programmed patrol pattern, engaging anyone who enters the zone, and nobody can issue a stand-down order.
Someone has hacked a Wolfhound's threat profile to add a specific individual's biometric data — the drone is hunting a person through a residential district.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact quadrupedal combat platform roughly the size of a large German Shepherd, with an aggressive forward-raked silhouette. The main body is a reinforced polymer/steel chassis mounted low between four articulated leg assemblies. A dorsal weapon pod houses the 5.56mm cannon; dual sensor turrets protrude from the forward section like predatory eyes. The overall impression is predatory and purposeful—a mechanical hunting animal.
physical_description.dimensions: Length: 85 cm (nose to tail), Height: 52 cm (at shoulder), Width: 48 cm (across leg stance), Barrel protrusion: 18 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty and solidly planted—35 kg of distributed mass feels grounded and immovable when stationary, but the weight is engineered for articulated agility rather than pure force
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced thermoplastic polymer chassis over a steel/titanium endoskeleton; weapon pod is hardened steel; leg joints are carbon-composite with steel articulation pins
physical_description.finish: Matte tactical black polymer body with brushed gunmetal steel accents on weapon hardpoints and sensor rings; scattered patches of micro-abrasion scarring from field deployment
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary matte black with gunmetal gray weapon pod and sensor turrets; amber LED indicator strips along spine; Sterling-Nakamura corporate silver trim around sensor housings
physical_description.grip_texture: Not handheld—vehicle interface via touchpad control unit or neural link; leg pads are textured non-slip polymer for urban surfaces
distinctive_features: Dual forward-mounted sensor turrets with concentric thermal/optical lens arrays—faintly glowing amber when active
Dorsal weapon pod with ribbed heat venting running the length of the spine
Four independently articulated legs with six-point load distribution, revealing joint hydraulics at flex points
Subtle red LED threat-indicator strip that pulses when autonomous engagement protocols are active
Reinforced nose cowl with integrated acoustic sensor array beneath polymer faring
Magazine feed access port along the left flank, barely visible in matte finish
Wear streaks and micro-abrasion patterns around the lower leg joints from rough-terrain navigation
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Sterling-Nakamura corporate emblem (interlocked double-helix) stamped in silver on both flanks; serial designation 'AHK-7' in white stencil on the rear chassis; FCC/regulatory compliance plates mounted horizontally on the right side in tiny font
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-deployed units show tactical wear—scuffed polymer, oxidized steel accents, dust accumulation in joint seams, occasional impact denting on the lower chassis; optical sensors appear perpetually alert and clean-maintained
